analysis.detail: Only custom ClientSessionStore implementations that format Tls12ClientSessionValue/Tls13ClientSessionValue with Debug leak secrets. lafiya-cli reaches rustls only through ureq (via lafiya-rpc-resilience), which uses rustls's built-in session cache whose Debug output is redacted; no code in the CLI implements or formats a ClientSessionStore. Contract wasm, npm packages and the indexer image do not contain rustls 0.23.45.

The leak happens only after a server rejects Encrypted Client Hello. ECH must be enabled explicitly with an EchMode in the rustls ClientConfig; ureq builds its ClientConfig without ECH and lafiya-cli does not supply its own TLS config, so the ECH code path is never entered.

The vulnerable Brotli certificate decompressor is behind the non-default rustls `brotli` feature. The resolved feature set for lafiya-cli is std, tls12, ring, log/logging (`cargo tree -p lafiya-cli -e features -i rustls`), so the decompressor is not compiled in.

The attack downgrades a client that prefers the X25519MLKEM768 post-quantum hybrid group to classical X25519. lafiya-cli uses the rustls `ring` crypto provider (no aws-lc-rs feature), which offers only classical key-exchange groups, so there is no hybrid preference to downgrade. Re-assess if the CLI ever switches to the aws-lc-rs provider.

Unmaintained-crate notice, not a vulnerability. paste is a proc-macro used by ark-ff under soroban-env-host, which is only pulled in by the soroban-sdk `testutils` feature. Proc-macros run at compile time and never ship: paste is absent from every release SBOM, including the contract wasm.
